title: Split pea and parsnip soup with crispy sprouts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Split peas, parsnips, onion, garlic, sprouts, oil, stock and lemon are all ordinary home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including yellow split peas, is an everyday item at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a heavy pan and a stick blender for the soup, which is allowed.

works.reason: 200g split peas with three parsnips in 1.2 litres of stock makes a sensibly thick soup for four, and 50 minutes to an hour is a fair time for the peas to collapse.

honest_times.reason: Halving the sprouts, chopping the veg and the 13 minutes of frying fit roughly within 25 minutes, and the 55-minute cook matches the simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and lemon, is used, and nothing unlisted appears in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: The Brussels sprouts are only a crispy topping on what is really a split pea and parsnip soup, so the hero ingredient is a garnish rather than the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling pulse and vegetable soup that a family would happily eat for lunch.
